item.title: Game Informer's Top Scoring Reviews Of 2026
item.description:
At Game Informer, writing game reviews is one of our primary functions. As such, we cover hundreds of titles each and every year, hoping to turn you on to your next favorite game. However, within that field, a select few rise to the top as the games we most highly recommend. While you're always welcome to peruse our reviews page for the latest and greatest (and sometimes worst) games on the market, we've gathered our highest-scoring reviews of 2026 right here. 

Be sure to bookmark this page and check back frequently, as we'll continue to update it as more titles earn review scores on the top end of our review scale.

10

Grand Theft Auto VI

Rockstar Games' latest release is a monumental achievement in storytelling, immersion, gameplay, and breadth of content. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S
Release Date: November 19, 2026

9.75

Resident Evil Requiem

A masterclass in refinement and a tour de force of gameplay, Requiem is Resident Evil at its finest. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PC
Release Date: February 27, 2026

9.5

Gears of War: E-Day

Gears of War: E-Day innovates in all the right ways while keeping the core and heart of the franchise intact, stamping the series’ return with one of, if not its best, entries to date. Read review

Platforms: Xbox Series X/S, PC
Release Date: October 6, 2026

Phantom Blade Zero

Though the action genre is always jam-packed with new releases, few are as special as Phantom Blade Zero. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, PC
Release Date: October 29, 2026

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter

Building on the already-great remake of the first game, Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter masterfully updates the gameplay and timeless story, adding up to what is now the Trails series’ defining entry, and one of the best RPGs of the year. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Switch 2, Switch, PC
Release Date: September 17, 2026

9.25

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a superb entry in the series, bringing Bandai Namco's aerial ballet to even higher heights. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC
Release Date: October 2, 2026

Cairn

Cairn is more than a remarkably gripping mountain-climbing game. It's also a deeply affecting narrative of anguish, loss, and the steep cost of obsession. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Switch 2, PC
Release Date: January 29, 2026 (PlayStation 5, PC), 2027 (Switch 2)

Castlevania: Belmont's Curse

Castlevania is back, and between Rose Belmont and Evil Empire, it's in great hands. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch, PC
Release Date: October 15, 2026

Forza Horizon 6

Even for a series built on delivering approachable racing action that appeals to both newcomers and hardcore players, Forza Horizon 6 impresses at each turn, delivering one of the greatest racing games of this generation. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC
Release Date: May 19, 2026 (Xbox Series X/S, PC), 2027 (PlayStation 5)

Marathon

Bungie’s excellent audio design and gunplay, paired with increasingly complicated level design borrowing from over a decade of expertise designing Destiny raids coalesce into something special. Marathon is proof Bungie is still at the top of its game. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC
Release Date: March 5, 2026

Saros

Moving, shooting, improving (both in stats and skill), winning, and even losing is an unequivocal joy, and I only wish I could write this final sentence faster so I can hurry up and get back to planet Carcosa and attempt another run. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5
Release Date: April 30, 2026

Super Mario Bros. Wonder Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Meetup in Bellabel Park

Super Mario Bros. Wonder was a joy to play through in 2023, and now, a few years later, it's even better. Read review

Platforms: Switch 2
Release Date: March 26, 2026

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026)

The 2026 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a fairly straightforward recreation. But an admittedly very good one. Read review

Platforms: Switch 2
Release Date: November 5, 2026

9

Big Walk

Big Walk is a lot of walking with your friends. Thankfully, it's a very good walk. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Switch 2, PC, Mac
Release Date: August 4, 2026

Deadzone: Rogue

Thanks to superb gunplay, a compelling mystery, and terrific use of the roguelite formula, Deadzone: Rogue avoids getting lost in the crowded sci-fi shooter genre. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PC
Release Date: August 11, 2025 (PC), September 3, 2025 (PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S), March 17, 2026 (Switch 2)

Final Fantasy Resonance

It may have one foot planted in the series' history, but in a time when mainline Final Fantasy is still figuring itself out, Final Fantasy Resonance is easy to recommend. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, Switch, PC
Release Date: October 22, 2026

Mixtape

Mixtape's stellar writing, concise runtime, and inspired use of its licensed soundtrack make it an instant classic and a heartfelt trip down memory lane. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PC, Mac
Release Date: May 7, 2026 (PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PC), October 28, 2026 (Mac)

Nioh 3

Nioh 3's consistently rewarding approach to open-world design, combined with its entertaining Ninja gameplay style, cements it as the best entry in the franchise. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, PC
Release Date: February 6, 2026

Paranormasight: The Mermaid's Curse

Paranormasight: The Mermaid's Curse is a brilliant modern adventure game, filled with mysteries, delightful characters, and gorgeous art. Read review

Platforms: Switch 2, Switch, PC, iOS, Android
Release Date: February 19, 2026

Pokémon Pokopia

Despite minor complaints, Pokémon Pokopia sticks out as one of the best examples of a third-party developer using the Pokémon license to the fullest extent possible. Read review

Platforms: Switch 2
Release Date: March 5, 2026

The Mermaid Mask

With memorable puzzles, eye-catching animations, and a spirited voice cast, I admire the way the story was told just as much as the story itself. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Switch 2, Switch, PC
Release Date: July 16, 2026

World of Warcraft: Midnight

Now more than ever, Azeroth feels like a home away from home. Read review

Platforms: PC, Mac
Release Date: March 2, 2026

8.75

007 First Light

Fantastic storytelling that captures the fun of the classic spy hero helps this new adventure shine bright. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PC
Release Date: May 27, 2026 (PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC), March 18, 2027 (Switch 2)

Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business

Though not every part lives up to the high bar set by its main gameplay, Australia Did It is ultimately defined by its creative combination mechanics, improvisational gameplay, and outstanding turn-based defense system. Read review

Platforms: PC
Release Date: November 17, 2026

Death Howl

Death Howl is a cohesive and well-crafted fusion of deckbuilders and Soulslikes. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch, PC
Release Date: December 9, 2025 (PC), February 19, 2026 (PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch)

Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave

Fortune's Weave is the latest entry in the Fire Emblem series, and it is both massive and worth the time investment. Read review

Platforms: Switch 2
Release Date: September 17, 2026

High On Life 2

High on Life 2 is the kind of game that you can put on, laugh at for a while, and forget what's troubling you, even though reminders might slip in through the pointed social commentary. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC
Release Date: February 13, 2026

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight

Even with my dissatisfaction with stealth and some minor glitches, the latest LEGO Batman is a rain-slicked success. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PC
Release Date: May 22, 2026 (PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC), September 18, 2026 (Switch 2)

Mina the Hollower

Mina the Hollower looks like a nostalgic throwback, and it undeniably is, but its thoughtful design and larger sensibilities make it play and feel like a contemporary video game – one that has taken the right lessons from the medium’s history. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, Switch, PC
Release Date: May 29, 2026

MIO: Memories in Orbit

Taking cues from the likes of Hollow Knight and Ori, this punishing platforming and exploration game is well worth your time if you're up for a big challenge. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, Switch, PC
Release Date: January 20, 2026

Splatoon Raiders

Though Splatoon’s single-player content has always been underappreciated, Splatoon Raiders makes it difficult to ignore, shining a bright light on the series’ oft-slept-on side. Read review

Platforms: Switch 2
Release Date: July 23, 2026

The Incident at Galley House

Unraveling the truth behind the unsolved deaths of a group of people gathering at a mansion one stormy night is engrossing and inventive, with a tale that keeps you guessing until its final moments. Read review

Platforms: PC
Release Date: July 14, 2026

8.5

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4

Backed up by a fun campaign, thrilling multiplayer, and loads of new modes and content, Modern Warfare 4 serves as a solid sendoff for the rebooted subseries. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PC
Release Date: October 23, 2026

Control Resonant

Despite fumbles with its new melee combat and difficulty balancing, Control Resonant's storytelling, world, and bizarre quests kept me eager to explore its distorted New York. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC, Mac
Release Date: September 24, 2026

Denshattack

Denshattack is weird as hell, and it leans into its strange premise with earned confidence, constantly building and layering on its ideas throughout at high speed. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PC
Release Date: July 15, 2026

Diablo IV: Lord of Hatred

Lord of Hatred is an exceptional cherry on top of Diablo IV, further cementing the entire package as among the best action RPGs of the generation. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, PC
Release Date: April 28, 2026

Dune: Awakening

Dune: Awakening succeeds in making players feel like everyone is out to get them, all while encouraging you to rise to the occasion and come out the other end stronger. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC
Release Date: June 10, 2025 (PC), September 22, 2026 (PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S)

Fur Squadron Phoenix

Nintendo may not know what to do with the Star Fox franchise, but Fur Squadron Phoenix makes a great case that the genre can still flourish in 2026. Read review

Platforms: Switch, PC
Release Date: February 18, 2026 (PC), February 25, 2026 (Switch)

Halo: Campaign Evolved

Even stripped of its multiplayer, this return trip to the original Halo nails the fun and chaos that made the series a landmark game. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC
Release Date: July 28, 2026

Invincible VS

With a solid foundation built upon approachability and personality, Invincible VS is easy to recommend to both seasoned fighting games fans and Invincible enthusiasts. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC
Release Date: April 30, 2026

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is a fighter that is as much of an advancement to the genre as it is an homage to the Marvel vs. Capcom era. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, PC
Release Date: August 6, 2026

Marvel's Wolverine

Insomniac once again captures what works about a famous comic book superhero, but that makes this a very different game from the studio's prior releases in the genre. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5
Release Date: September 15, 2026

Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy

Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy executes familiar genre staples and delivers a moving story starring a charismatic pirate on what may be the most impactful and tragic adventure of her life. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC
Release Date: August 27, 2026

Star Wars: Galactic Racer

Galactic Racer is a Star Wars game, and that might be enough for some, but not for me. Fortunately, it's an even better racing game. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC
Release Date: October 6, 2026

Tenebris Somnia

Tenebris Somnia's effective blend of classic adventure game design and live-action filmmaking results in a captivating, spooky, and well-crafted adventure. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch, PC
Release Date: October 16, 2026

Void/Breaker

Though it can be difficult at times, if you can see through the literal remains of your destruction, one of the year's most engaging shooters awaits. Read review

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC
Release Date: November 4, 2026

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Review - Outrageous Fortune
item.description:
Reviewed on: PlayStation 5
Platform: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S
Publisher: Rockstar Games
Developer: Rockstar Games
Release: November 19, 2026

Many superlatives will be heard in the discussion around Grand Theft Auto VI – biggest world, most activities, best graphics, deepest narrative – but its real triumph is the way all those features and others work in service of a cohesive, believable immersion in a criminal fantasy that is hard to grasp until you’ve played it for yourself.

Grand Theft Auto VI – Video Review:

Rockstar’s latest returns players to a dramatically expanded version of the Vice City seen in a prior game, now largely unrecognizable after real and in-game years have passed. Leonida is a joy to explore, filled with a wealth of activities, both mundane and illicit. The game’s design makes many ordinary tasks as compelling as the illegal ones. Go fishing off the boat, brew coffee to wake up, work out at the gym, scuba dive for long-lost treasure, dust crops, motocross in the mud, go dancing at the club. As you move between those activities, the world feels alive with minor events, from traffic accidents to shady individuals a little too interested in your walk to the ATM. GTAVI delights in life's minutiae, with animations, voice lines, and background characters that keep things fresh even dozens of hours into the story. The level of detail everywhere is astounding and, at times, overwhelming. Getting sidetracked is easy.

The focus on detail carries into the visuals. Lucia’s hair blows in the wind, and she absently pushes it back behind her ear. A drug den is littered with paraphernalia and empty containers. A shifty contact quirks a smile – your only hint that things are about to go south. Sweat glistens on your character’s skin after a hard workout, their breathing and heart rate noticeably heightened. Clouds roll together in the sky, creating realistic weather simulations. The commitment to an authentic simulated world is encompassing, thoughtful, and intentional, a testament to hand-crafted and meticulously painstaking development work, paying off in an absorbing play-space that is hard to step away from.

While the day-to-day simulation is fascinating, it also adds pacing and counterpoint to the explosive march of major missions, narrative threads, and set-piece encounters that drive the game forward. Not even one of these meticulously choreographed sequences deserves to be spoiled; they run the gamut from amusing shenanigans at a strip club to intense chases and escapes fueled by raging gunfights and explosions. Many of the best moments leverage an expert sense of musical accompaniment, weaving a slick original score alongside one of the most impressive and wide-ranging licensed soundtracks ever heard in a video game – often to surprisingly emotional effect.

 

Ranged combat is punchy and enjoyable; smart use of cover and time-slowing focus makes most battles manageable. On-foot navigation is in a similar boat – simple to pick up and uninterested in needless complexity or challenge; the focus is on choosing smart moments for stealth, knowing when to run and when to fight, and selecting the precise instant for a burst of sudden action. Driving is fast and intense, made more appealing by a huge variety of functionally distinct vehicles to enjoy. If there’s a fault to the core and optional story missions, it’s that many feel a bit on rails regarding where to go and what to do at each step. At the same time, that directed approach keeps the pace relentless, and the action and outcomes thrilling. Over many hours, the game morphs and throws new wrenches into the mix at key junctures, teasing and then playing out criminal experiences from petty theft to group heists to illicit spec ops, and punctuates those distinct vibes with memorable and singular moments.

Like its predecessors, GTAVI simultaneously lampoons and celebrates life in modern America, taking aim at targets like social media, wellness lifestyles, rap and music culture, manosphere content, and dozens more. The caricatures land so well because, in many cases, they’re (sadly) barely over the line of the absurdity we see reflected in real life, and because Rockstar so ably captures individual subcultures, dialects, and situations. Behind it all is a scathing critique of wealth inequality and the inherent unfairness of a system that sets most up to fail. It’s a bitter message delivered in honey-wrapped, exhilarating gameplay, but it shines through.

Of all its significant feats, the relationship between Lucia and Jason elevates the game to new heights, lending this installment a heart, tension, and emotional core missing from prior entries. This is, without a doubt, video gaming’s most richly drawn and compelling romance, featuring two leads who are immediately relatable and compelling to watch. Player actions dictate the strength of their bond, deepening the sense of engagement. Like the best crime fiction, you’re left surprised by how much you cheer for two people who regularly commit terrible acts. The two collectively suffer the slings and arrows of a world that always seems stacked against them; the fortune they amass is not a power grab, but a desperate attempt to cling to each other and come out the other side together, and the player can’t help but cheer them on and dread how fate might stand in the way.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a generational game that stands toe-to-toe with many of the great crime stories and satires across other media. It showcases both the entertainment value of interactive play and the current high-water mark for technical and artistic detail in games. Hunt for and count up all the minor faults or foibles you like, but then note how you just spent another hour lost in this remarkable escape into criminality, wanton violence, egregious sex, and the elusive potential of true love.

Score: 10

item.title: Civilization Developer Firaxis Lays Off A Third Of Its Staff
item.description:
Firaxis, the studio behind the Civilization series, has laid off around 60 employees, representing a third of its staff. The report comes from Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier.

In a statement provided to Bloomberg by a spokesperson from 2K, a subsidiary of Firaxis' owner, Take-Two, “Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength—designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years. As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”

In addition to the 60 affected staffers, Firaxis studio head Heather Hazen is also departing. Bloomberg also reports, via anonymous Firaxis employees speaking to the outlet, that the studio is working on an unannounced XCOM game that has had a challenging development, with the team recently missing an important development milestone. This project, if it releases, will be the first Firaxis-developed XCOM game since XCOM: Chimera Squad in 2020.

Firaxis’ most recent release is Civilization VII, which launched in February 2025 to favorable reviews but initially "slow" sales, according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick last August.  The game currently has a Mixed reception on Steam after Firaxis spent the last year updating the game to address player complaints. Before Civilization VII, Firaxis shipped Marvel's Midnight Suns in 2022, another critically well-received game that failed to meet sales expectations. 

[Source: Bloomberg]
